articles.title: CNOOC Ltd Production Hits Historic High
articles.description: CNOOC Ltd said the first three quarters of 2026 delivered the company's highest-ever net production for the January-September period at 593.7 million barrels of oil equivalent, up 2.7 percent from the same period last year.

articles.title: Poland Expands Gas Storage Capacity by a Quarter
articles.description: ORLEN completed a $153.44-million expansion of the Wierzchowice Underground Gas Storage Facility, increasing the capacity of Poland's largest gas storage site to 74.2 billion cubic feet.

articles.title: Oil Sector Girds for Possible Windfall Tax
articles.description: The oil industry is bracing for Democrats to use their newfound political muscle to push for a deal with President Donald Trump and impose a windfall tax.

articles.title: ADNOC, ADQ Chemicals JV Secures Additional $1.39B Financing
articles.description: TA'ZIZ, tasked with establishing a 'world-scale chemicals and transition fuels ecosystem' in the Ruwais Industrial City in the United Arab Emirates, finalized $1.39 billion in additional financing to support two of its projects.

articles.title: Aramco Looks to Strengthen Supply Network, CEO Reveals
articles.description: Aramco's CEO announced that the company is continuing to 'explore additional overseas storage capacity', as well as 'alternative export routes', in order to 'further strengthen' Aramco's global supply network.

articles.title: BP Reduces Stake in Norwegian Producer
articles.description: BP sold a five percent stake in Aker BP for around $1.06 billion, part of the British company's efforts to free up cash.

articles.title: Oil Prices Tumble After Midterms
articles.description: Oil prices 'tumbled' eight percent yesterday following the U.S. midterm elections, Saxo Bank highlighted.

articles.title: EU Not Planning to Resume Russian Gas Purchases
articles.description: The European Union neither wants nor has any plans to resume purchases of Russian gas, EU diplomats told EUobserver as European, U.S., and Ukrainian officials are meeting in Brussels to discuss post-war recovery in Ukraine ahead of next week’s US-Ukraine-Russia negotiations in Abu Dhabi. “We don’t see any rationale at the moment to ease sanctions or restrictions on Russia, in any sector,” an EU diplomat told EUobserver. “On the contrary, in light of the barbaric and cynical attacks on Ukrainian civilians and…

articles.title: Iran Braces for Trump's Next Move After Democrats Sweep Congress
articles.description: The landslide victory by Democrats in US midterm elections is expected to bring change to Congress and foreign policy in Washington. But inside Iran, many officials said they expect the country will remain in the crosshairs of President Donald Trump, even if the vote has left him weaker. As the results poured in late on November 3, showing Democrats had taken control of both the House of Representatives and Senate from their Republican rivals, Trump admitted the war he launched on Iran on the last day of February had taken a toll on his party.…

articles.title: Worley signs EPC contract for Venture Global’s CP2 expansion project
articles.description: Worley has been awarded a reimbursable EPC contract by Venture Global for the CP2 expansion project, a LNG export facility in US.

articles.title: Dangote’s fuel storage and pipeline project in Namibia breaks ground
articles.description: Dangote Group has broken ground on a fuel storage and regional pipeline project valued at $2.5bn in Walvis Bay, Namibia.

articles.title: IEEFA: $67.8 Billion in Asian LNG Power Projects Scrapped or Stalled
articles.description: More than half of proposed LNG-to-power projects, worth a total of $67.8 billion, in four key Southeast Asian markets have been either scrapped or stalled since 2021, amid rising costs that raise risks for project financing, the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA) said in a report on Thursday. The five-year analysis of $109.2 billion worth of proposed LNG-fired power projects and another $21 billion worth of planned LNG import terminals in the Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, and Bangladesh showed that as many as 49 proposed…

articles.title: European Gas Prices Drop on Iran Deal Hopes after U.S. Midterms
articles.description: The benchmark European natural gas prices fell by 2% in the early morning in Amsterdam on Thursday, extending Wednesday’s decline, after the resounding Democratic victory in the U.S. midterm elections raised hopes of a resolution to the Iran war and a return of LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz. The front-month price at the Dutch Title Transfer Facility (TTF), the benchmark for Europe’s gas trading, fell by 2.2% as of 9 a.m. in Amsterdam on Thursday, as energy markets hope the path forward to the Iran war could be pursuit…

articles.title: Woodside to Cut Over 500 Jobs
articles.description: Australia's largest natural gas producer said it would cut about 11 percent of its workforce as it targets $400 million of annual cost reductions from 2028.

articles.title: Pentagon Eyes Unprecedented 75-Year Deal to End China's Rare Earth Stranglehold
articles.description: The U.S. Army wants first dibs on American-produced heavy rare earths, and REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY) has just signed a landmark nonbinding term sheet that could put it at the top of the military's supply chain list. And the terms are extraordinary. The term sheet proposes a potential 75-year operating lease on approximately 200 acres at Tooele Army Depot in Utah, where REalloys would build and operate a facility processing dysprosium and terbium, two metals China has spent decades monopolizing. In return, one of the things that the Army wants is…

articles.title: UK government to ban new North Sea oil and gas licences
articles.description: The UK government has announced the introduction of the Energy Independence Bill, which aims to prohibit the granting of new licences for oil and gas exploration in the North Sea.

articles.title: India to Require State Utilities to Add Energy Storage Capacity
articles.description: India plans to soon mandate state-owned utilities to add energy storage capacity to take advantage of the clean energy boom with reduced waste of generated power amid lagging storage capacity, a senior official said on Thursday. India’s federal authorities will require the state utilities to add storage capacity, Pankaj Agarwal, secretary of the Indian Power Ministry, said at the ongoing Bharat Renewable Energy Summit. India is working to launch additional clean energy tenders for energy storage, the official added. Grid, flexibility, and…

articles.title: Iran Reports More Tanker Fires in Strait of Hormuz
articles.description: Two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Thursday, as Iran continues to report a growing number of incidents with vessels trying to transit the Strait on routes unauthorized by the Islamic Republic. One of the oil tankers hit a naval mine while it was attempting to move south of the Strait. Another tanker caught fire as it was on its way out in the eastern part of the Strait, and a tugboat that had approached it to help also caught fire, according to Iran’s…

articles.title: China’s Diesel Exports Set to Plunge as Domestic Inventories Run Low
articles.description: China’s diesel exports are on track to drop in November from the highs seen in August and September as increased fuel shipments at the end of the summer dented domestic inventories, traders and executives with knowledge of this month’s export plans told Reuters on Thursday. So far this month, Chinese refiners have sold about 500,000 metric tons of diesel for November loading, according to estimates by Reuters and trade sources. Refiners are yet to finalize deals for loading in the second half of November, but early estimates show the…

articles.title: SOCAR Bets $1.65 Billion on U.S. Shale Gas Boom
articles.description: Azerbaijan’s state oil and gas company SOCAR has struck a deal with Comstock to acquire some of its assets in the Haynesville shale and an infrastructure subsidiary. The price tag of the deal is $1.65 billion. The purchase includes a 20% stake in Comstock’s legacy Haynesville assets, a 15% stake in Western Haynesville, and 15% of Comstock’s majority interest in gas infrastructure subsidiary Pinnacle Gas Services. The deal comes amid widely shared expectations of extended growth in global demand for natural gas and U.S. growth…

articles.title: EU Survey Reveals Massive Support for Renewable Energy Transition
articles.description: A majority of European Union citizens are in favor of an accelerated transition away from oil and gas and into alternative energy sources and transport electrification, a survey conducted by the European Investment Bank has shown, as reported by Reuters, which got an exclusive look at the survey. According to the survey, which involved 23,000 respondents, 87% wanted governments to make the transition a priority, with 52% saying solar should be at the top of the list of alternative, low-carbon energy sources. articles.title: Oil Prices Continue to Fall as Democratic Sweep Shakes Energy Markets
articles.description: Crude oil prices moved even lower, and energy company stocks followed after the results of the U.S. midterms, as markets brace for a potentially radical change in U.S. policies. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $94.30 per barrel, after dropping by 9% on Wednesday, and West Texas Intermediate was trading at $87.35 per barrel, after shedding 8% on Wednesday, following the Democrats’ majority in both houses. articles.title: Oil Plunges as Election Shifts Iran Outlook
articles.description: Oil prices tumbled as political pressure mounted to end the war and restore energy flows.

articles.title: UAE Mulls 3rd Crude Oil Pipeline to Avoid Hormuz
articles.description: The United Arab Emirates is considering a third oil-export pipeline that will deliver crude outside the Strait of Hormuz, according to people familiar with the matter.
